target: नर्स ने मरीज़ को दवाई खिलाई।
english: The nurse gave the patient medicine.
tip: दवाई खिलाई (davaaee khilaaee) is literally 'fed the medicine' – खिलाना (khilaanaa) means making someone eat. In Hindi, patients are fed medicine, not given it.

target: ढोल बजाकर समारोह शुरू किया गया।
english: They started the ceremony by beating the drum.
tip: The ending -कर (-kar) means 'having done it': ढोल बजाकर (dhol bajaakar = having beaten the drum). One small ending does the work of English 'by ...ing'.

target: अनिल ने बाज़ार से ताज़ी मछली ख़रीदी।
english: Anil bought fresh fish from the market.
tip: ख़रीदी (khareedee) ends in -ee because मछली (machhlee = fish) is feminine – with ne the verb matches the thing bought, not the buyer. Anil's own gender never touches it.

target: पैंसठ साल की उम्र में वे रिटायर हो गए।
english: He retired at the age of sixty-five.
tip: One respected man, plural verb: वे रिटायर हो गए (ve retire ho gaye = they retired) said of a single person. Respect turns he into they, and the verb agrees.

target: मेरे नाना-नानी ने बहुत मुश्किल वक़्त देखा है।
english: My maternal grandparents have seen very hard times.
tip: नाना-नानी (naanaa-naanee) means specifically your mother's parents – your father's are दादा-दादी (daadaa-daadee). Hindi has no plain 'grandparents'; the side always shows.

target: नाविक ने नाव खेते हुए नदी पार की।
english: The boatman crossed the river rowing the boat.
tip: -ते हुए (-te hue) = 'while doing': नाव खेते हुए (naav khete hue = while rowing the boat). Two actions in one sentence, no word for 'while' needed.

target: मैंने वेटर से बिल माँगा।
english: I asked the waiter for the bill.
tip: You ask FROM someone: वेटर से बिल माँगा (vetar se bil maangaa = asked the bill from the waiter). माँगना (maangnaa = ask for) always takes se, never ko.

target: जिस किसान ने सिंचाई की, उसकी फ़सल अच्छी हुई।
english: The farmer who irrigated had a good crop.
tip: Hindi pairs its linking words: जिस किसान ने (jis kisaan ne = the farmer who) opens, उसकी (uskee = that one's) answers. English drops the second half – Hindi says both.

target: मैंने पहली बार दक्षिण भारतीय डोसा खाया और बहुत पसंद आया।
english: I ate South Indian dosa for the first time and liked it very much.
tip: You don't 'like' things in Hindi – they come to your liking: पसंद आया (pasand aayaa = came to liking). The dosa does the arriving; you just receive it.

target: मैंने कल अपना मोबाइल रिचार्ज कराया।
english: I recharged my mobile yesterday.
tip: कराया (karaayaa) = got it done by someone else: रिचार्ज कराया (recharge karaayaa) – the shop recharged it, I arranged it. किया (kiyaa) would mean I did it myself.

target: दुकानदार ने सामान जल्दी भेज दिया।
english: The shopkeeper sent the goods quickly.
tip: भेज दिया (bhej diyaa) adds देना (denaa = give) to 'sent' – the give part marks the job fully done, aimed at someone else. A bare भेजा (bhejaa) feels unfinished.

target: सुनीता ने मेहमानों के लिए मिठाई परोसी।
english: Sunita served sweets to the guests.
tip: के (ke) + a word builds two-part position words: के लिए (ke liye = for), as in मेहमानों के लिए (mehmaanon ke liye = for the guests). Learn each pair as one chunk.

target: मैंने ऑटो वाले को पचास रुपये दिए।
english: I gave the auto driver fifty rupees.
tip: वाला (vaalaa) turns any noun into 'the one with it': ऑटो वाले (auto vaale) = the auto guy. Chai vaalaa, rickshaw vaalaa – it names people by what they run.

target: ब्लड प्रेशर की जाँच नियमित करवाओ।
english: Get your blood pressure checked regularly.
tip: करवाओ (karvao) = have it done by someone else: जाँच नियमित करवाओ (jaanch niyamit karvao) = get the check-up done regularly. Doing it yourself would be करो (karo).

target: चारों बच्चे मिलकर खेल रहे हैं।
english: All four children are playing together.
tip: A number plus -ों makes 'all of them': चारों बच्चे (chaaron bachche) = all four children, दोनों (donon) = both. English needs the extra word 'all'.

target: ऑटो वाले ने मीटर नहीं लगाया।
english: The auto driver didn't use the meter.
tip: वाला (vala) turns a noun into 'the one with it': ऑटो वाले ने (auto vale ne) = the auto guy did. Same trick everywhere – चाय वाला (chai vala) = the tea seller.

target: औज़ार रखने के लिए लोहे का बक्सा चाहिए।
english: An iron box is needed for keeping tools.
tip: No verb 'to need' – the needed thing is the subject: बक्सा चाहिए (baksa chahiye = a box is needed). The person who needs it takes को (ko).

target: अभी बारिश हो रही है, छाता ले लो।
english: It is raining right now, take an umbrella.
tip: छाता ले लो (chhata le lo): the extra लो (lo) marks doing it for yourself. दे दो (de do) would mark doing it for someone else. Hindi tags who benefits.

target: आँगन में चारपाई बिछाकर बैठो।
english: Lay out the cot in the courtyard and sit.
tip: Hindi chains actions with -कर (kar = having done): बिछाकर बैठो (bichhakar baitho) = having spread it, sit. English says 'lay it out AND sit' – Hindi drops the 'and'.

target: और, क्या हाल है? सब ठीक है ना?
english: How are you? Is everything okay?
tip: One little ना (na) does all of English's tag questions: सब ठीक है ना? (sab theek hai na?) covers 'isn't it', 'right?', 'aren't you' – no matching verb needed.

target: शोभा पार्क में दौड़ रही है।
english: Shobha is running in the park.
tip: English -ing never changes, but रही (rahi) does: Shobha gets दौड़ रही है (daud rahi hai) because she's female – a man would be दौड़ रहा है (daud raha hai).

target: नमस्कार, मैं डॉक्टर शर्मा बोल रहा हूँ।
english: Namaskaar, this is Doctor Sharma speaking.
tip: Phone Hindi skips 'this is' – you say who you are directly: मैं डॉक्टर शर्मा बोल रहा हूँ (main Doctor Sharma bol raha hoon = I am Doctor Sharma speaking).

target: डॉक्टर मरीज़ को देख रहे हैं, थोड़ा रुकिए।
english: The doctor is seeing a patient, please wait a bit.
tip: One doctor, plural verb: respect turns देख रहा है (dekh raha hai) into देख रहे हैं (dekh rahe hain). Elders, doctors and bosses get the plural form even when they're one person.

target: बच्चे छत पर पतंग उड़ा रहे हैं।
english: Children are flying kites on the terrace.
tip: उड़ाना (udana) means 'make fly': kids are पतंग उड़ा रहे हैं (patang uda rahe hain), making the kite fly. Plain उड़ना (udna) is what the kite itself does.

target: मैं हिंदी सीख रहा हूँ, कृपया धीरे बोलिए।
english: I am learning Hindi, please speak slowly.
tip: -इए is the respectful command: धीरे बोलिए (dheere boliye = please speak slowly). बोलो (bolo) is the plain version you'd use with friends.

target: अरे वाह, कितने दिनों बाद मिल रहे हैं!
english: Oh wow, meeting after so long!
tip: मिलना (milna) means both 'meet' and 'get'. Here मिल रहे हैं (mil rahe hain) = we're meeting; but पानी मिल रहा है (paani mil raha hai) would mean water is available.

target: मैं तीन महीने से हिंदी पढ़ रहा हूँ।
english: I have been studying Hindi for three months.
tip: For 'I have been studying', Hindi uses the present continuous plus से (se = since): तीन महीने से हिंदी पढ़ रहा हूँ (teen mahine se hindi parh raha hoon).

target: ताऊजी आँगन में कुर्सी पर बैठे अख़बार पढ़ रहे हैं।
english: Uncle is sitting on a chair in the courtyard reading the newspaper.
tip: 'Is sitting' is NOT बैठ रहे (baith rahe) – that means in the act of sitting down. The seated state uses बैठे (baithe): बैठे अख़बार पढ़ रहे हैं (baithe akhbaar parh rahe hain) = seated, reading.

target: जैसे-जैसे शहर बढ़ रहा है, प्रदूषण भी बढ़ रहा है।
english: As the city grows, pollution keeps rising too.
tip: Doubling जैसे-जैसे (jaise-jaise) means 'as... steadily': जैसे-जैसे शहर बढ़ रहा है (jaise-jaise shahar barh raha hai) = as the city keeps growing.

target: बाहर बूँदा-बाँदी हो रही है।
english: It is drizzling outside.
tip: No dummy 'it' for weather – rain and drizzle just happen: बूँदा-बाँदी हो रही है (boonda-baandi ho rahi hai = drizzle is happening).
